findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, ENOENT).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire thread instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError>. Use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| BudgetError::Io(e))? and propagate.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing into a dynamically-sized Vec. If the line lacks a comma, parts.len() == 1 and parts[1] panics.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input (missing delimiter) causes a panic instead of a recoverable parse error.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (name, value_str) safely. Check the Option and return a typed ParseError on None.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input in the value field.
findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric budget value crashes the thread. The caller has no way to skip or report the bad record.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get value_str, then value_str.parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| BudgetError::Parse(e))? to return a typed error.

findings.problem: Lossy as cast: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates any value > 65535.
findings.failure_mode: Budget values in range 65536..=4294967295 wrap around, corrupting the budget data without any error indication. This is a data-integrity violation.
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 via parse::<u16>(), or use u32::try_from(value).map_err(|_| BudgetError::Overflow) if u32 parse is needed first.

findings.problem: println!() inside the parsing map closure mixes side-effect I/O into what should be a pure data-loading path.
findings.failure_mode: Side effects in the core parsing pipeline make the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and produce stdout pollution that cannot be suppressed during testing.
findings.fix: Remove the println!. If logging is needed, push a debug/info tuple into the returned Records or handle it exclusively in the imperative shell layer that calls this function.

findings.problem: Function signature pub fn load_budgets(path: &str) -> Vec<Record> hides all failure modes. Every I/O operation, every parse, and every indexing can fail, but none are expressed in the return type.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot handle or distinguish between file-not-found, parse failure, type overflow, or malformed lines. The function silently panics on any error path.
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_budgets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is a typed enum covering Io, Parse, and MalformedLine variants.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line when only the first two fields are needed.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line (alloc + dealloc + string clone) degrades throughput. The skill explicitly requires split_once for first-delimiter extraction.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract (name_part, value_part). Trim each part as &str, then convert only the two needed fields.

findings.problem: No try_reserve or bounded capacity handling before collecting into Vec. If the file has many lines, unbounded allocation can OOM.
findings.failure_mode: Large files cause unbounded memory allocation with no error handling. Allocation failure returns OOM panic rather than a typed error.
findings.fix: Count lines or use an initial capacity estimate, then use Vec::with_capacity or try_reserve before collecting. Handle AllocationError by returning a typed BudgetError::Allocation(e).

no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis of the parsing path
no allocation tracing (e.g., dhat-rs, alloc-count) for per-line Vec<String> overhead
no second-ring evidence (assembly, allocator stats) for claimed zero-cost or low-allocation behavior
no command-level evidence: cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run during this review
residual_risk: All eight findings are BLOCKER-level. Every code path in load_budgets can panic. The function must be rewritten with typed errors, split_once, checked arithmetic, try_reserve, and no println! in the core before this crate can be considered compliant with Holzman Rust.
